entries.promptHtml:
coolcool
schoolschoolschoolschool
entries.prompt: COOL twice, then SCHOOL four times
entries.joke: What do you call a fish with no eyes? Fsh.
entries.discuss: If you found $10 and nobody claimed it, what would you do with it, and why?

bright.title: X-rays work in space
bright.blurb: Astronauts took the first medical X-rays in orbit, a step toward keeping people healthy on the way to the Moon.

entries.prompt: What has keys but can't open a door?
entries.joke: Why did the golfer bring two pairs of pants? In case he got a hole in one.
entries.discuss: Can two things share a name and still be nothing alike? What other words work that way?

bright.title: A robot turtle that hunts plastic
bright.blurb: A high-schooler built a swimming robot turtle that uses AI to spot tiny bits of plastic in lakes and rivers.

entries.prompt: A farmer has 17 sheep. All but 9 die. How many are left?
entries.joke: How do you organize a space party? You planet.
entries.discuss: What food makes you feel ready to think, and what food makes you sleepy?

bright.title: Turning mosquito bites into practice
bright.blurb: Scientists are testing a way to stop malaria early so later mosquito bites help the body learn, instead of making people sick.

entries.promptHtml: deal
entries.prompt: DEAL in very large letters
entries.joke: What do you call a snowman in summer? A puddle.
entries.discuss: What makes something a big deal to one person and nothing to another?

bright.title: Small towns getting hospital tools
bright.blurb: The same portable X-ray kit that worked in orbit is the kind of tool that could help clinics far from a city hospital.

entries.prompt: What can you catch but not throw?
entries.joke: Why was 6 afraid of 7? Because 7 8 9.
entries.discuss: When does moving your body feel like play, and when does it feel like a chore?

bright.title: Learning that does not need a building
bright.blurb: More families are piecing together a school day from parks, kitchens, and one hard question, and the work still counts.

entries.promptHtml: lifeoncetime
entries.prompt: ONCE sitting in the middle of LIFETIME
entries.joke: Why did the scarecrow win an award? He was outstanding in his field.
entries.discuss: Should you wait for a once-in-a-lifetime moment, or make ordinary days count more?

bright.title: Satellites that find their own way
bright.blurb: A NASA swarm learned to figure out where it is by looking at other objects in space, not just by asking Earth.

entries.prompt: I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?
entries.joke: What do you call a fake noodle? An impasta.
entries.discuss: How is a map true, and how is it a lie?

bright.title: A whole generation of young inventors
bright.blurb: Kids around the world are building robots and medical ideas at kitchen tables, then showing them at science fairs.

entries.prompt: A snail climbs 3 feet up a 10-foot well each day and slides 2 feet down each night. On which day does it get out?
entries.answer: Day 8 (on day 8 it climbs the last 3 feet from 7 to 10 and is out before night)
entries.joke: Why don't scientists trust atoms? They make up everything.
entries.discuss: Would you rather have $20 today or $30 next month? What changes your answer?

bright.title: More driverless taxis on city streets
bright.blurb: In a few cities you can hail a car with no one behind the wheel, and the service is opening to more riders.

entries.promptHtml: CYCLECYCLECYCLE
entries.prompt: CYCLE CYCLE CYCLE
entries.joke: What did the ocean say to the beach? Nothing, it just waved.
entries.discuss: What does a prefix tell you before you even know the whole word?

bright.title: Hearing that starts from the inside
bright.blurb: Researchers are testing gene therapy that tries to repair the inner ear itself, not only amplify sound from the outside.

entries.promptHtml: STANDI
entries.prompt: STAND with I under it
entries.joke: Why did the math book look sad? It had too many problems.
entries.discuss: If you cooked supper for someone you love, what would be on the plate, and why those things?

bright.title: Clean water from unlikely places
bright.blurb: New filters and sun-powered stills are pulling safe drinking water from dirty sources and even from the air.

entries.prompt: What has to be broken before you can use it?
entries.joke: What do you call a bear with no teeth? A gummy bear.
entries.discuss: What else in life has to break a little before it becomes useful?

bright.title: Kids building the next tools
bright.blurb: This year’s student science fairs were full of robots and medical ideas invented at kitchen tables and in garages.

entries.prompt: It takes 12 minutes to saw a log into 4 pieces. How long to saw it into 6 pieces? (equal pieces, same saw)
entries.answer: 20 minutes (3 cuts for 4 pieces, 5 cuts for 6)
entries.joke: Why can't your nose be 12 inches long? Because then it would be a foot.
entries.discuss: What's a kind of tired that feels good, and how is it different from the worn-out kind?

bright.title: Rockets that come home again
bright.blurb: Boosters that land and fly again are making it cheaper to send telescopes, weather tools, and people off the planet.

entries.promptHtml: WEARLONG
entries.prompt: WEAR with LONG under it
entries.joke: What do you call cheese that isn't yours? Nacho cheese.
entries.discuss: How do you untangle a picture-puzzle when the words feel in the wrong order?

bright.title: Farm robots that weed and pick
bright.blurb: In more fields, small robots now spot weeds and ripe fruit so farms can grow food with a lighter touch.

entries.promptHtml: TOUCHDOWN
entries.prompt: TOUCH then D-O-W-N stacked as a column
entries.joke: Why did the bicycle fall over? It was two-tired.
entries.discuss: Why do games and stories need a clear we-made-it moment?

bright.title: A planet-hunter waits on the pad
bright.blurb: NASA’s Roman telescope is aimed at launch, ready to hunt for worlds we have never seen with a camera that drinks in a wide sky.

entries.prompt: What gets wetter the more it dries?
entries.joke: What's orange and sounds like a parrot? A carrot.
entries.discuss: When is it smart to wait to buy something, and when is waiting just frustrating?

bright.title: Robots that could reach a stroke in time
bright.blurb: Engineers are building remote helper-robots so a life-saving stroke treatment might one day reach people far from a big hospital.

entries.prompt: A bat and a ball cost $1.10 in total. The bat costs $1.00 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?
entries.joke: Why did the student eat his homework? The teacher said it was a piece of cake.
entries.discuss: Why does the obvious first answer feel so sure even when it is wrong?

bright.title: Coral that can take the heat
bright.blurb: Reef teams are growing corals that handle warmer water, so color and fish can return to tired reefs.

entries.promptHtml: GROUNDFEETFEETFEETFEETFEETFEET
entries.prompt: GROUND with six FEET under it
entries.joke: What do you call a sleeping bull? A bulldozer.
entries.discuss: When is a treat a treat, and when is it just habit?

bright.title: A school day that looks like a quest
bright.blurb: Homeschool is getting better at feeling like a project, not a desk: one problem, real tools, and time to finish it.

entries.prompt: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?
entries.joke: Why are ghosts bad liars? You can see right through them.
entries.discuss: What do you leave behind that you never notice?

bright.title: New pictures of old light
bright.blurb: The James Webb Space Telescope keeps sending back galaxies and planet weather from so far away the light is ancient.

entries.promptHtml: HIGHandLOW
entries.prompt: HIGH above and LOW below the word and
entries.joke: What do you call an alligator in a vest? An investigator.
entries.discuss: If you invented a game that made people run without calling it exercise, what would it be?

bright.title: Houses printed from a nozzle
bright.blurb: Giant 3D printers are laying down walls in days, a way to build sturdy homes with less leftover scrap.

entries.prompt: 3 cats catch 3 mice in 3 minutes. How many cats to catch 100 mice in 100 minutes? (same rate)
entries.joke: Why did the cookie go to the nurse? It felt crummy.
entries.discuss: If you triple the time, do you always need to triple the workers? When would that fail?

bright.title: A clue in the back of the eye
bright.blurb: A 17-year-old built an AI tool that studies a photo of the retina, looking for patterns that might help kids get support sooner.

entries.promptHtml: HEADHEELS
entries.prompt: HEAD stacked over HEELS
entries.joke: Why did the stadium get hot after the game? All the fans left.
entries.discuss: When have you been so into something that everything else felt small for a while?

bright.title: Paper that folds into a working robot
bright.blurb: Engineers are making flat sheets that fold themselves into tiny machines, the kind of trick that could one day tuck tools into a pocket.

entries.prompt: What has a head, a tail, is brown, and has no legs?
entries.joke: What do you call a dinosaur that is always on time? A prompt-saurus.
entries.discuss: Would you rather get $20 once, or $2 every day for two weeks? Why?

bright.title: Clean water from salty waves
bright.blurb: New desalting setups use less power to turn ocean water into drinking water, a quiet win for towns that live near the coast.

entries.prompt: A drawer has many red and blue socks mixed up. How many socks must you pull (in the dark) to be sure you have a matching pair?
entries.joke: Why don't eggs tell jokes? They'd crack each other up.
entries.discuss: When is 'just in case' smart, and when is it just packing too much?

bright.title: Batteries that last longer between charges
bright.blurb: Labs keep finding ways to pack more energy into the same size battery, so phones, bikes, and tools can go farther on one charge.

entries.promptHtml: MINDMATTER
entries.prompt: MIND stacked over MATTER
entries.joke: What did the grape do when it got stepped on? It let out a little wine.
entries.discuss: What meal would you invent if the only rule was that it had to make people talk at the table?

bright.title: Hearing aids that learn your day
bright.blurb: Newer hearing tools can tune themselves to a noisy room or a quiet talk, so more people can join the conversation without strain.

entries.promptHtml: LINESREADINGLINES
entries.prompt: READING between the LINES
entries.joke: How do you make a tissue dance? Put a little boogie in it.
entries.discuss: When has someone said one thing out loud but meant something else underneath?

bright.title: A second chance for leftover wood
bright.blurb: Small shops and makers are turning scrap lumber into furniture and toys, proving leftover material can still become something people love.

entries.prompt: I'm light as a feather, yet the strongest person can't hold me for five minutes. What am I?
entries.joke: Why did the belt go to jail? It held up a pair of pants.
entries.discuss: What is a kind of practice that feels hard in the moment but good afterward?

bright.title: Learning that feels like finishing a quest
bright.blurb: More families are treating school like a project board: one hard problem, real tools, and a finish you can show someone.

entries.prompt: If 5 machines make 5 widgets in 5 minutes, how long do 100 machines take to make 100 widgets (same rate)?
entries.joke: What do you call a pig that does karate? A pork chop.
entries.discuss: When does adding more people make a job faster, and when does it just make a crowd?

bright.title: Satellites that watch wildfire smoke
bright.blurb: New orbit cameras track smoke plumes in near real time, helping crews see where air is getting thick before people feel it.

entries.promptHtml: LOOKbeforeLEAP
entries.prompt: LOOK before LEAP
entries.joke: Why did the tomato turn red? Because it saw the salad dressing.
entries.discuss: When is it wise to pause, and when does pausing just mean you never start?

bright.title: Vaccines that train the body faster
bright.blurb: Researchers keep finding sharper ways to teach the immune system, so protection can show up sooner against tough bugs.

entries.prompt: What is full of holes but still holds water?
entries.joke: What do you call a boomerang that won't come back? A stick.
entries.discuss: Is it better to save first and spend later, or buy something you need now and catch up later?

bright.title: Concrete that can heal its own cracks
bright.blurb: Scientists are mixing tiny helpers into concrete so small cracks can seal themselves, which could make bridges last longer.

entries.promptHtml: FORGIVEN
entries.prompt: FOR next to GIVEN
entries.joke: Why was the broom late? It over-swept.
entries.discuss: What does it take to forgive someone, and what does it take to feel forgiven?

bright.title: A telescope that will map dark sky
bright.blurb: Teams are finishing giant surveys that will chart billions of galaxies, a map of how the universe grew over time.

entries.prompt: How many times can you subtract the number 5 from 25?
entries.joke: What kind of key opens a banana? A mon-key.
entries.discuss: What snack actually helps you keep going, and what snack just makes you want another snack?

bright.title: Farms that waste less water
bright.blurb: Smart drips and soil sensors are helping growers give plants only what they need, so more food grows with less waste.

entries.promptHtml: TIMEafterTIME
entries.prompt: TIME after TIME
entries.joke: Why did the computer go to the doctor? It had a virus.
entries.discuss: What is something you got better at only because you did it again and again?

bright.title: Robots that sort recycling better
bright.blurb: AI arms on sorting lines can spot plastics and metals faster than a busy conveyor allows, so less good material ends up in the trash.

entries.prompt: What runs but never walks, has a bed but never sleeps, and has a mouth but never eats?
entries.joke: Why can't you give Elsa a balloon? Because she will let it go.
entries.discuss: If your perfect Saturday had to include moving your body somehow, what would the day look like?

bright.title: Medicine printed one pill at a time
bright.blurb: 3D printers are starting to make pills shaped for one person, so a dose can match a kid's size instead of a one-size bottle.

entries.promptHtml: BJACKOX
entries.prompt: JACK inside BOX
entries.joke: Why did the kid bring a ladder to school? Because it was high school.
entries.discuss: What surprise is fun, and what surprise is the kind that makes you jump for the wrong reason?

bright.title: Kids teaching machines to be kinder
bright.blurb: Classrooms are trying simple AI helpers that practice patience and clear questions, a peek at tools that work with kids, not at them.
